title: Falsification-Oriented Scoping Review of Typed-Interface Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

# Falsification-Oriented Scoping Review of Typed-Interface Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

## Executive summary

### Bottom line

**I did not find primary prior work that is identical to the complete TI-MARL/PILS concept as you currently define it. However, a broad claim such as “a new MARL architecture for heterogeneous agents with changing observation/action spaces, parameterized actions, safety, and coordination” would not be defensible.** Nearly every major ingredient already has strong prior art, and several recent papers come uncomfortably close to important subsets of the idea. The scientific opportunity, if it survives implementation and experiments, appears to lie in a **specific integration and formalization of runtime typed interfaces**, not in Transformers, parameterized actions, action masking, variable agent populations, safety projection, or optimization-based coordination individually. citeturn14view8turn17search0turn21view0turn16view1turn21view5

The specification I evaluated is the one you provided: an agent has a runtime schema describing role, modules, observations, actuators/action ports, constraints, health and dependencies; that schema induces typed observation parts and parameterized action ports; a shared policy reasons over the current interface rather than a fixed vector; sensor health can contract the interface; and local proposals are subsequently coordinated under shared physical and community constraints. fileciteturn0file0

My present assessment is:

| Claim | Falsification result | Confidence |
|---|---|---:|
| **N1 — runtime schema induces typed observations + parameterized action ports** | **PARTIAL OVERLAP** | Medium-high |
| **N2 — policy selects/parameterizes current runtime action ports** | **STRONG SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP** | High |
| **N3 — observation health/dependencies change port validity/bounds** | **ADJACENT BUT DISTINCT** | Medium |
| **N4 — interface expansion/contraction + population changes without rebuilding policy layout** | **STRONG SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP** | High |
| **N5 — local proposals become jointly feasible, utility-aware actions** | **STRONG SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP** | High |
| **N6 — coordinator balances local/community utility, fairness, urgency and policy deviation** | **STRONG SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP** | High |
| **N7 — same interface contract supports learning, compatibility, deployment, fail-safe and versioning** | **STRONG SUBSTANTIAL OVERLAP**, especially after 2026 systems work | Medium-high |
| **N8 — typed interface yields faithful execution-level explanations** | **ADJACENT BUT DISTINCT** | Medium |

The most important finding is therefore **not** “TI-MARL is novel.” It is this:

> **The literature appears to contain the pieces, but I did not locate a primary method in which a machine-readable runtime interface is itself a first-class policy input and operational contract that causally determines both a variable set of typed observation entities and a variable set of semantically typed, parameterized action ports—with explicit observation-health/action-validity dependencies—and then carries those same typed resource couplings into multi-agent joint feasibility/allocation and deployment compatibility.**

That sentence is currently a **candidate research gap**, not a novelty claim. The distinction matters.

The strongest threats are particularly clear:

**Headless-AD** already shows a single Transformer model generalizing to previously unseen discrete action spaces whose *size, semantic content, and order* change. This directly invalidates any claim that simply “being able to act over variable semantic action sets without retraining the output head” is new. citeturn14view8

**Compositional Interfaces** already separates observation modules, a shared controller, and action modules, and generalizes to unseen combinations of observation and action spaces. Therefore “one controller across different observation and action interfaces” is also not new. citeturn14view9

**Shared Modular Policies** goes further back: a single policy can control morphologies whose state and action dimensionalities change, using actuator-associated modules and local sensors with message passing. citeturn17search0

**CrossFormer** uses the same network weights across 20 robot embodiments with widely different sensors, actuators, and control frequencies, without manual observation/action-space alignment, including real-world evaluation. That is a serious counterexample to weak formulations of “heterogeneous interfaces.” citeturn21view2

**MOHITO** is perhaps the closest MARL threat to dynamic actions: it explicitly formalizes a **task-open Markov game** in which tasks—and consequently actions—change dynamically, and uses dynamically evolving hypergraphs to represent relationships among agents, tasks, and actions. citeturn21view0

**UAS/U-MAPPO** explicitly reasons about heterogeneous *action semantics*, constructs a union action space, and uses per-agent available-action masks. It is not what you propose—it remains a fixed global superset—but it would be a mandatory baseline because it represents the obvious simpler alternative to typed ports. citeturn20view0

**Safe MARL shielding**, **MADDPG safety layers**, cooperative **CBF + differentiable QP**, and **ReCoDe** already establish that learned multi-agent actions can be corrected or constrained after policy inference to satisfy joint safety/coordination requirements. Therefore the final “JCP” layer is not intrinsically novel. citeturn16view0turn16view1turn16view2turn15view6

Finally, 2026 work on **ECM Contracts** and **Governed Capability Evolution** is especially important for the deployment side. ECM Contracts encode functional signatures, behavioral assumptions, resources, permissions, recovery semantics and version compatibility, and perform compatibility checking before installation/composition/upgrades. Governed Capability Evolution adds interface/policy/behavioral/recovery compatibility checks, sandboxing, shadow deployment, gated activation, monitoring and rollback. Neither appears to integrate these ideas into MARL policy observation/action semantics, but they sharply reduce any standalone novelty claim around “versioned machine-readable capability contracts.” citeturn14view0turn14view4

### The promising scientific nucleus

After trying to falsify the idea, I would **narrow the target** from:

> “TI-MARL handles heterogeneous and reconfigurable MARL.”

to something closer to:

> **Contract-conditioned reconfigurable MARL in which a runtime typed interface is a first-class component of the decision process: the interface compiler maps capabilities, observation provenance/health, dependencies and physical constraints into variable typed observation tokens and parameterized action ports; a shared policy reasons directly over that current interface; and resource-coupling metadata is preserved into joint multi-agent feasibility and allocation.**

Even that needs experimental evidence before being called novel.

The architecture that best survives the review is approximately:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Runtime Agent Schema]
    H[Health / validity / capabilities]
    C[Interface Compiler]
    O[Typed Observation Parts]
    P[Typed Action Ports]
    E[Set / Graph / Transformer Encoder]
    PS[Port Selector]
    PD[Port-specific Parameter Decoder]
    LP[Local Action Proposal + Utility]
    JC[Joint Feasibility & Allocation Coordinator]
    FS[Runtime Safety / Fallback]
    A[Executed Actions]

    S --> C
    H --> C
    C --> O
    C --> P
    O --> E
    P --> E
    E --> PS
    PS --> PD
    PD --> LP
    P --> JC
    LP --> JC
    JC --> FS
    FS --> A
```

Crucially, **the arrows from `health → interface compiler → action validity/bounds` and from `typed resource coupling → joint coordinator` are more scientifically distinctive than the neural encoder itself.**

## Search protocol and conceptual boundaries

This was conducted as a **falsification-oriented scoping review**, not a systematic meta-analysis. The objective was to locate the strongest prior studies capable of defeating each of N1–N8 rather than accumulate papers that merely support the motivation.

The search covered influential earlier work and literature available through **August 2026**, emphasizing primary papers and official proceedings from ICML/PMLR, ICLR, CoRL, UAI/AISTATS, AAMAS, L4DC, arXiv for recent work, and official author/code resources. Recent 2026 preprints were retained where they materially affect novelty, but their unreviewed status is explicitly relevant to confidence. citeturn19search0turn14view0turn14view4

Search families included parameterized/hybrid actions; variable and unseen action sets; action embeddings; action primitives; modular and cross-embodiment control; heterogeneous MARL; open-agent/open-task systems; dynamic populations; graph/set/Transformer policies; action masking; constrained MARL; shielding and QP/CBF safety; joint resource allocation; fairness; sensor-failure robustness; runtime assurance; compositional policy systems; interface/version contracts; and explainability by structured decision traces.

The inclusion rule was deliberately broad across domains. Energy/RECs were the intended application, but robotics and general CPS were included because the core methodological question concerns changing sensors, actuators, capabilities, physical constraints and agent populations. This proved essential: some of the strongest challenges to TI-MARL come from robotics rather than energy. citeturn17search0turn21view2turn18search0

The key distinction used throughout the review is:

\[
\text{changing vector dimension}
\neq
\text{changing action cardinality}
\neq
\text{changing action semantics}
\neq
\text{changing typed runtime interface}.
\]

For example, masking actions from a known fixed union is materially different from receiving a runtime object that says:

```text
port:
    type: EV_CHARGE
    parameters:
        power:
            unit: kW
            dynamic_bounds: [0, 6.4]
    requires:
        - EV_CONNECTED
        - SOC
    resource_coupling:
        site_import_capacity: +power
    valid: true
```

UAS represents semantically distinct actions through a fixed union and availability masks; Headless-AD accepts varying semantic discrete actions; P-DQN/HyAR represent discrete action types with continuous parameters; RAPS exposes manually defined parameterized primitives. None of those facts alone establishes that a typed port contract of the form above is novel, but they tell us exactly what cannot be claimed. citeturn20view0turn14view8turn21view5turn21view6turn21view4

Similarly, “dynamic agents” was not treated as equivalent to “dynamic interfaces.” Open ad hoc teamwork methods already support agents entering/leaving, while task-open MARL already supports dynamically changing actions. The harder potential gap is **simultaneous population reconfiguration and within-agent capability/interface reconfiguration under one policy abstraction**. citeturn18search2turn21view1turn21view3turn21view0

### Limitations of this review

This is not evidence that no earlier paper exists. Terminology is fragmented across MARL, robotics, hybrid control, safe RL, software architecture and CPS; relevant work may describe similar mechanisms as affordances, capabilities, skills, modular control, resource contracts or action schemas rather than “typed interfaces.” Recent 2026 work is particularly fluid. Furthermore, some broad candidates were screened from abstracts and official paper pages rather than reconstructed line-by-line from implementations.

Industrial systems, patents and unpublished/internal platforms were not exhaustively searched. Formal-methods and software-contract research was searched primarily where it intersects learned controllers; a full programming-languages/interface-theory review could uncover additional N7 precedents.

Accordingly:

> **“No close primary evidence found” must never be converted into “first ever.”**

## Taxonomy and closest prior art

The neighboring literature falls into several distinct families. TI-MARL only has a chance of being interesting if it occupies an intersection rather than relabeling one of them.

### Parameterized and semantic actions

P-DQN established deep RL for discrete-continuous hybrid actions by combining discrete action choice with continuous action parameters. MP-DQN refined the parameterized-action Q-network mechanism; HyAR learns a compact latent representation encoding the dependence between discrete action and continuous parameters; and DLPA applies model-based planning to Parameterized Action MDPs. These works are direct prior art against any claim that “port selection + a parameter head” is new. citeturn21view5turn20view4turn21view6turn17search10

RAPS is even more conceptually relevant because it explicitly argues that the **interface between RL and the robot** matters: it manually specifies a library of transferable action primitives parameterized by policy-generated arguments. citeturn21view4

The difference that might remain is that TI-MARL ports are proposed to be **runtime objects**, with their own semantic type, unit, parameter schema, dynamic bounds, validity dependencies, health requirements and shared-resource effects. The parameterized-action literature normally assumes that the action types and their parameterization structure are part of the predefined problem formulation. citeturn21view5turn21view6

### Variable action spaces and compositional interfaces

The strongest direct threat to N2 is Headless-AD. It is trained once and then acts over discrete spaces whose **size, semantic content and order vary**, including action spaces unseen in training. Therefore a fixed output dimension is demonstrably unnecessary even without typed interfaces. citeturn14view8

Jain, Szot and Lim had already formalized zero-shot generalization to new actions in 2020 using learned action representations and policies flexible to changing action sets. citeturn17search1

In 2026, *Online Decision Making with Generative Action Sets* goes further in a different direction: the action set itself can expand online as the agent chooses to create new reusable actions. This is an online-learning formulation rather than TI-MARL, but it makes any generic claim around “expanding action spaces at runtime” unsafe. citeturn19search0turn19academia14

Compositional Interfaces is equally important for the input/output side. It uses space-specific differentiable observation and action modules around a shared controller and demonstrates generalization to unseen combinations of observation, action and instruction spaces. citeturn14view9

### Modular and cross-embodiment control

Shared Modular Policies attaches identical neural modules to actuators; each receives local sensor information, modules communicate, and a single policy handles agent morphologies for which both state and action dimensionality vary, including unseen variants. citeturn17search0

CrossFormer is a much stronger modern reference point. The same weights operate across 20 robot embodiments with widely different sensors, actuators and control frequencies, and the system does not require manual alignment of observation or action spaces. Its evaluation includes real robots. citeturn21view2

Therefore the contribution cannot simply be:

> “One network can work with different sensors and actuators.”

That problem has substantial prior art.

The potentially meaningful difference is:

> “The controller does not merely normalize heterogeneous embodiments; it consumes an explicit runtime contract that defines what information and control affordances currently exist, why they are valid, and how they participate in physical constraints.”

### Heterogeneous, open and task-open MARL

UAS is a particularly relevant baseline because it explicitly treats **action semantics** as a source of physical heterogeneity. Its solution constructs the union of all actions and generates heterogeneous policies using available-action masks; U-MAPPO and U-QMIX retain global parameter sharing. citeturn20view0

This is close conceptually but also highlights a clean difference:

```text
UAS
all possible actions known globally
        ↓
fixed semantic superset
        ↓
mask unavailable actions

TI-MARL candidate
runtime capabilities discovered/described
        ↓
current typed ports instantiated
        ↓
policy scores current candidate set
```

That difference must be experimentally justified. If fixed-superset masking performs just as well and has acceptable scaling, the typed-port architecture risks being only a cleaner software abstraction.

Open ad hoc teamwork has already removed the fixed-population assumption. GPL supports agents with different fixed policies entering and leaving without notice; CIAO builds on graph-based policy learning for unrestricted numbers and types of teammates. citeturn18search2turn21view1

Transferable MARL with Dynamic Participating Agents explicitly studies CTDE with agents joining and leaving during training and reports rapid adaptation for new agents. citeturn21view3

MOHITO is even closer to your conceptual direction: in a task-open Markov game, tasks appear/disappear and **the action space itself changes dynamically**; the actor-critic architecture uses evolving hypergraphs over agents, tasks and actions. citeturn21view0

Official implementation verified during this review:

- [MOHITO official repository](https://github.com/oasys-mas/mohito-public) citeturn15view0
- [CIAO experimental repository](https://github.com/hsvgbkhgbv/CIAO), linked by the ICML paper. citeturn21view1
- Shared Modular Policies links its code/project from the ICML proceedings page. citeturn17search0

### Safe action correction and resource coordination

Safe MARL via Shielding synthesizes a centralized shield that observes joint actions and corrects unsafe ones, with a factored variant for scalability. This is a direct counterexample to any basic “multiple local actions are checked jointly before execution” novelty claim. citeturn16view1

Safe MADDPG adds a safety layer to continuous-action multi-agent policies and performs an action-correction step under constraints. citeturn16view0

Cooperative CBF MARL integrates cooperative safety constraints through a differentiable QP layer; it additionally uses conformal prediction to qualify uncertainty in surrounding-vehicle behavior. citeturn16view2

ReCoDe is conceptually important because it combines MARL and decentralized optimization: agents use local communication to collectively impose dynamic constraints on their allowed actions, and the work reports both theoretical and real-robot evidence. citeturn15view6

Fair resource allocation in weakly coupled MDPs directly addresses sequential decisions in which resource constraints couple otherwise independent sub-MDPs, and optimizes fairness using a generalized Gini objective. This significantly weakens any claim that adding fairness to shared resource allocation is itself novel. citeturn16view3

### Robust sensing and deployment contracts

Sensor Dropout already showed in 2017 that an RL policy can remain functional under partial sensor failure. More recent masked multimodal training explicitly targets deployed robot policies robust to missing sensor modalities and evaluates multiple embodiments in simulation and the real world. citeturn18search8turn14view10

What I did **not** find in these works is the stronger mechanism you proposed:

```text
SoC sensor HEALTHY
    → discharge port valid
    → bound = [0, 6 kW]

SoC sensor STALE
    → discharge port retained
    → conservative bound = [0, 1 kW]

SoC sensor FAILED
    → discharge port invalid
    → reason = REQUIRED_STATE_UNAVAILABLE
```

The robust-sensor literature generally makes policies tolerate missing/corrupted inputs rather than explicitly compile sensor health into the semantics and feasible domain of action capabilities. citeturn14view10turn18search8

For deployment, however, the 2026 systems literature is a substantial warning. ECM Contracts represents capability-module contracts beyond simple type signatures, including resource requirements, recovery semantics and version compatibility, and checks compatibility before deployment. Governed Capability Evolution adds lifecycle-time interface, policy, behavior and recovery checks together with shadow deployment, monitoring and rollback. citeturn14view0turn14view4

Those are not presented as MARL learning interfaces—the ECM Contracts page does not even identify reinforcement learning as its framing—but they mean that “versioned capability contract + compatibility checking + recovery semantics” cannot safely be claimed as a new concept in isolation. citeturn14view0turn14view1

Two observations emerge from the matrix.

First, **no single retained paper spans all columns**. The closest works are complementary rather than identical: MOHITO dominates dynamic MARL actions; Headless-AD dominates variable semantic action sets; Compositional Interfaces/CrossFormer/SMP dominate changing embodiments/interfaces; P-DQN/HyAR/RAPS dominate parameterized actions; safety/shielding/QP work dominates post-policy feasibility; and ECM Contracts/Governed Capability Evolution dominate deployment contracts. citeturn21view0turn14view8turn14view9turn21view2turn21view5turn16view1turn14view0

Second, that does **not** imply that simply connecting all these blocks produces scientific novelty. “A system that combines known techniques” needs either a new formal problem, a new algorithmic coupling, a demonstrably new capability, or compelling empirical evidence that the integration solves a problem existing formulations cannot solve.

### What has definitely been falsified

Several possible weak novelty claims should now be abandoned.

**“A policy can work with variable action spaces.”** False as a novelty claim. Headless-AD explicitly does this with varying semantic content and unseen action spaces; earlier work addresses new-action generalization as well. citeturn14view8turn17search1

**“Agents can join and leave without reconstructing a fixed-size centralized model.”** Not novel. Open ad hoc teamwork and dynamic-participating-agent work explicitly target changing populations. citeturn18search2turn21view3

**“MARL can have dynamically changing actions.”** Not novel. MOHITO's task-open Markov-game formulation addresses dynamically changing action spaces. citeturn21view0

## Method-design implications, experiments and kill tests

### Recommended formalization

I would stop treating “TI-MARL” merely as an architecture and first define a formal decision process. A provisional name such as **Typed-Interface Markov Game (TIMG)** remains useful.

A conventional Markov game has a largely static definition of agents, observation mappings and action spaces. Your extension should make the interface itself time varying:

\[
\mathcal G =
\left\langle
\mathcal S,
\{\mathcal I_t\},
\{\Sigma_{i,t}\},
P,
P_{\Sigma},
R,
\gamma
\right\rangle ,
\]

where \(\Sigma_{i,t}\) is the runtime interface schema of agent \(i\).

Rather than defining a permanent vector \(o_i\) and permanent action space \(\mathcal A_i\), define an interface compiler:

\[
\mathcal C:
(\Sigma_{i,t}, h_{i,t}, s_t)
\mapsto
\left(
\mathcal O^{\text{parts}}_{i,t},
\mathcal P_{i,t},
D_{i,t},
B_{i,t},
M_{i,t}
\right),
\]

with:

- \(\mathcal O^{\text{parts}}_{i,t}\): current typed observation parts;
- \(\mathcal P_{i,t}\): current action ports;
- \(D_{i,t}\): observation/action dependency relations;
- \(B_{i,t}\): dynamic parameter bounds;
- \(M_{i,t}\): validity and health metadata.

An action port is **not an action**. It is a typed callable control capability:

\[
p =
(\tau_p,\Theta_p,U_p,B_p,V_p,D_p,C_p,E_p),
\]

where, provisionally:

- \(\tau_p\): semantic action type;
- \(\Theta_p\): parameter schema;
- \(U_p\): units;
- \(B_p\): bounds;
- \(V_p\): validity predicate;
- \(D_p\): dependency requirements;
- \(C_p\): shared-resource coupling;
- \(E_p\): optional physical-effect description/model.

Then the policy acts over the **current set**:

\[
\pi_\theta
\left(
p,\eta_p
\mid
\mathcal O^{\text{parts}}_{i,t},
\mathcal P_{i,t},
\Sigma_{i,t}
\right),
\]

rather than:

\[
\pi_\theta(a_i\mid o_i)
\quad
\text{for fixed }a_i\in\mathbb R^d.
\]

This mathematical distinction is important because Headless-AD, UAS, P-DQN and MOHITO force you to be very precise about what is actually different. citeturn14view8turn20view0turn21view5turn21view0

### The neural architecture should not be the principal novelty claim

A tokenized Set Transformer/Transformer/GNN is a sensible engineering choice, but not a strong novelty target. Graph policies already handle variable agent sets, Transformer policies already handle variable semantic actions, and cross-embodiment policies already consume heterogeneous inputs/outputs. citeturn18search2turn14view8turn21view2

A sound architecture would be:

\[
z^{obs}_k = E_{\tau_k}(x_k,m_k),
\]

\[
z^{port}_p = E^A_{\tau_p}(\text{schema}_p),
\]

\[
Z_i =
F_\theta
\left(
z_i^{self},
\{z^{obs}_k\},
\{z^{port}_p\},
z_i^{community}
\right),
\]

followed by candidate scoring:

\[
\ell_{i,p}
=
g_\theta(Z_i,z^{port}_p),
\]

\[
\Pr(p\mid i,t)
=
\operatorname{softmax}_{p\in\mathcal P_{i,t}^{valid}}
(\ell_{i,p}),
\]

and port-conditioned parameters:

\[
\eta_{i,p}
=
d_{\tau_p}
(Z_i,z^{port}_p),
\qquad
\eta_{i,p}\in B_{i,p,t}.
\]

That resembles prior parameterized-action and variable-candidate mechanisms by design; the intended contribution is the **contract semantics feeding them**, not inventing softmax over candidates. citeturn21view5turn14view8

### The joint layer should be formulated as allocation, not merely safety

Your `0.6 + 0.6 > 1.0` example becomes scientifically clearer if the final layer is explicitly separated from the policy.

Suppose local policies propose:

\[
\tilde{\mathbf a}
=
(\tilde a_1,\ldots,\tilde a_n).
\]

A joint coordinator could solve:

\[
\mathbf a^*
=
\arg\max_{\mathbf a}
\left[
\sum_i
U_i(a_i \mid z_i)
+
\lambda U_C(\mathbf a)
-
\mu
D(\mathbf a,\tilde{\mathbf a})
-
\rho
\Phi_{\mathrm{fair}}(\mathbf a)
\right]
\]

subject to:

\[
a_i\in \mathcal A^{valid}_{i,t},
\]

\[
g_k(s_t,\mathbf a)\le 0,
\]

\[
h_l(s_t,\mathbf a)=0.
\]

For two chargers:

\[
a_1+a_2\le1.
\]

But the solution need not be:

\[
(0.5,0.5).
\]

If agent two has imminent departure and agent one does not, a utility-aware solution might be:

\[
(0.3,0.7),
\]

assuming local bounds permit it.

This is a much better conceptual model than “safe clipping.” However, the literature says clearly that **the optimization layer itself is not enough for novelty**: joint shielding, CBF/QP layers, dynamic constraints and fair coupled-resource optimization already exist. citeturn16view1turn16view2turn15view6turn16view3

A better provisional name than `JCP` would therefore be something explicit such as:

> **Joint Feasibility and Allocation Layer (JFAL)**

or

> **Joint Constraint and Utility Coordinator (JCUC)**.

The first is more neutral.

### Baselines that would be mandatory

A credible experiment cannot compare only against PPO/MATD3/MADDPG. The novelty question demands **structural baselines**.

For interface handling, the most important baseline is a **fixed universal/padded action and observation space with masks**, conceptually corresponding to UAS. If your typed interface cannot beat or materially simplify this baseline under substantial reconfiguration, the central architectural argument weakens. citeturn20view0

For dynamic candidates, compare against a candidate-action representation inspired by **Headless-AD/new-action generalization**, particularly when testing unseen ports or action semantics. citeturn14view8turn17search1

For parameterized actions, compare with **P-DQN/MP-DQN/HyAR-style** mechanisms where applicable. citeturn21view5turn20view4turn21view6

For heterogeneous interfaces, compare against a **modular controller** in the style of Shared Modular Policies or Compositional Interfaces. citeturn17search0turn14view9

For dynamically changing actions/tasks, **MOHITO** should be treated as a serious conceptual baseline or at least a methodological reference. citeturn21view0

For variable populations, use a graph/set MARL baseline and open-team reference such as GPL/CIAO. citeturn18search2turn21view1

For joint feasibility:

```text
No coordination
Clipping
Equal/proportional allocation
Minimum-deviation QP projection
Centralized shield
CBF/QP safety layer
Utility-aware QP/MILP coordinator
```

are more informative than only comparing return against MARL algorithms. The shield/QP literature establishes these as meaningful alternatives. citeturn16view1turn16view2

For sensor failures, compare:

```text
zero/default imputation
mask bit only
history/recurrent estimator
Sensor Dropout-style training
typed dependency-based interface contraction
```

because robust missing-sensor policies already exist. citeturn18search8turn14view10

### Ablations that determine whether TI-MARL is actually doing anything

The critical ablations are not “two layers versus three layers.” They should test the proposed scientific mechanism.

**Schema semantics:** remove semantic type metadata while retaining raw values.

**Dependencies:** remove observation-to-action dependency relationships.

**Health:** retain missingness masks but disable health-induced action contraction.

**Dynamic bounds:** retain action ports but replace their runtime bounds with global static bounds.

**Typed action ports:** replace candidate ports with one fixed padded action superset plus masking.

**Port embeddings:** identify each action only through an integer ID.

**Parameter decoder:** shared generic parameter decoder versus type-specific decoder.

**Runtime unseen composition:** hold out combinations such as `[EV + battery + heat pump]` during training while each constituent capability is seen separately.

**Unseen port type:** much harder and potentially much more significant—introduce a genuinely unseen action type whose semantics/schema make transfer theoretically possible.

**Population reconfiguration:** join/leave agents while simultaneously changing asset interfaces.

**Health reconfiguration:** sensor degradation while controlling a resource needed by multiple agents.

**Coordinator:** no coordinator versus projection-only versus utility-aware allocation.

**Fairness:** coordinator without fairness versus explicit fairness.

**Policy-deviation penalty:** remove \(D(a,\tilde a)\) and measure how often coordination destroys learned intent.

**Resource-coupling metadata:** remove port-declared couplings and reconstruct constraints using hand-coded asset IDs; this tests whether the schema actually buys generality.

**Deployment compatibility:** deliberately deploy a policy against incompatible schema versions and test pre-execution rejection.

These experiments determine whether the idea is a new learning method or merely a good software API.

### The kill list

The project should be radically reformulated if any of the following occurs.

**A close prior paper is found that already formalizes a runtime schema generating both typed observations and parameterized action candidates, including dynamic validity/dependencies.** That would directly threaten N1–N3.

**A MOHITO-like method is found that additionally supports within-agent capability/sensor/action-schema reconfiguration and dynamic agent populations.** That would erase much of the formal-problem novelty. MOHITO already handles task-driven changing action spaces in MARL. citeturn21view0

**The fixed-superset masked baseline matches TI-MARL across all reconfiguration tests.** In that case, typed ports may still be valuable engineering, deployment and explainability machinery, but a new MARL algorithm claim becomes difficult.

**The method requires retraining whenever a previously unseen schema combination appears.** Then its “runtime interface” claim becomes much weaker because Compositional Interfaces and Headless-AD already demonstrate meaningful unseen-interface/action generalization. citeturn14view9turn14view8

**The method only works for ports whose identity was present during training.** It can still solve changing availability, but should not be marketed as open-ended typed-interface generalization.

**Sensor health is just a mask feature fed to the neural network.** Then N3 collapses toward existing sensor-failure robustness. The stronger concept requires health/dependency semantics to have an explicit operational effect on action validity or bounds. citeturn14view10

**The joint layer is simply a standard QP minimizing distance to proposed actions.** Useful, but not a novel algorithmic contribution given existing action correction and differentiable QP safety. citeturn16view0turn16view2

**Adding utility/fairness terms does not improve service quality or constraint allocation over simple proportional/priority heuristics.** Then N6 is unnecessary complexity.

**Safety is claimed only because training exhibits few violations.** If Safety is one of the thesis-level properties, the system should clearly separate learned performance from enforceable feasibility/fallback behavior.

**The explanation consists only of attention weights.** That would miss the strongest advantage of typed interfaces. The explanation should come from the actual validity predicates, bounds, selected port, resource constraints and optimizer modifications.

**Deployment contracts are separately implemented metadata rather than the same semantics used by the learning interface.** Then N7 becomes largely conventional MLOps/runtime assurance, an area already strongly occupied by recent contract/governance work. citeturn14view0turn14view4

## Recommended scientific position and novelty map

### Minimal defensible claim

At this stage, I would **not** state:

> “We introduce a novel TI-MARL architecture for heterogeneous and dynamic multi-agent systems.”

That is too broad and vulnerable.

The strongest *minimal candidate claim* I would design the method around is:

> **We study multi-agent decision problems in which an agent's observation and control interface is itself a time-varying structured object. We represent that interface through a machine-readable schema and a deterministic interface compiler that maps runtime capabilities, observation provenance/health, semantic dependencies and physical constraints into variable sets of typed observation entities and parameterized action ports. A shared policy operates directly over the compiled interface rather than a predeclared fixed action-vector layout.**

Even this should currently be labeled a **candidate contribution**, because the search found substantial adjacent work but cannot prove absence of identical prior art. The distinction from Compositional Interfaces, Headless-AD, MOHITO, UAS, RAPS and CrossFormer would have to be made explicitly. citeturn14view9turn14view8turn21view0turn20view0turn21view4turn21view2

I would make the coordination layer a **supporting mechanism**, not part of the minimal novelty claim:

> Local policy proposals are resolved against typed shared-resource couplings using a joint feasibility/allocation layer.

That is scientifically useful, but existing shielding, QP, decentralized-constraint and fair-allocation work makes it a poor standalone novelty claim. citeturn16view1turn16view2turn15view6turn16view3

### Stronger claim if experiments succeed

A genuinely stronger result would be:

> **A single contract-conditioned MARL policy can preserve competent and safe behavior under simultaneous changes in agent population, observation availability, sensor health, installed capabilities and parameterized action interfaces—including held-out combinations—without rebuilding its global observation/action layout; typed resource-coupling information additionally enables policy-independent joint feasibility and utility-aware allocation under shared CPS constraints.**

That would be much more compelling because it is an **empirical capability claim**, not a claim that individual architectural components are new.

An even stronger paper would demonstrate:

\[
\text{trained schemas}
\rightarrow
\text{held-out compositions}
\rightarrow
\text{runtime capability change}
\rightarrow
\text{sensor degradation}
\rightarrow
\text{agent join/leave}
\rightarrow
\text{shared-resource conflict}
\]

in the **same experiment**, while a fixed masked architecture, standard heterogeneous MARL, parameterized-action RL and modular policy baselines fail or degrade substantially.

### Recommendation on TI-MARL versus PILS

After this review, I would **keep TI-MARL as the working research name** and postpone attaching PILS to the algorithm.

“Typed Interface” describes the component that appears to have the clearest possible scientific differentiation. “Physics-informed” is much harder to defend unless physical models genuinely alter representation, inference, feasible-set construction or learning—not merely because a QP enforces power limits.

> **“Can the typed interface be made into a genuinely new decision-process abstraction that gives measurable zero-/low-shot reconfiguration, robustness, safety and scaling advantages over fixed masking, modular policies, open-agent MARL and parameterized-action methods?”**

If the answer to that question becomes yes experimentally, there is a credible research contribution. If not, the typed interface may still be an excellent systems architecture for EnergAIze—but it should not be presented as a new MARL method.
